channelReport.body_md:
# Channels spike (P-005): measured, not adopted

Plan `client-native-features-adoption-2026-10-21`, item P-005, Decision `client-native-features-adoption-2026-10-21#D-013`. Measured 2026-10-21 on Claude Code 2.1.293.

Correction (2026-10-22): the earlier 43 ms figure used the wrong event boundary. The saved native debug log explicitly starts engine turn 1 at 19:40:13.595Z, 77 ms after the server emit. No adoption conclusion changes. See plan D-016.

## Verdict

**Do not adopt Channels as the coord wake transport now.** Keep the prototype emitter (`packages/operator-core/lib/channels/coord-channel-emitter.ts`, tested against the CLI's own message schema) so a later adoption starts from a verified shape.

## What Channels is (read from the installed CLI)

- A channel is an MCP server that declares `capabilities.experimental["claude/channel"]`.
- It pushes `notifications/claude/channel` with `{ content: string, meta?: Record<string,string> }`. The CLI drops every meta key that is not `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`.
- The CLI turns each push into a queued prompt `<channel source="…" key="value">content</channel>` with priority `next`. It runs as the next turn and never interrupts a running one. The turn is marked `isMeta` with origin `{kind: "channel"}`.
- Registration is skipped unless all of these hold: the server is named in `--channels` (a bare `server:` entry also needs `--dangerously-load-development-channels`; a plugin entry needs the approved allowlist); the provider is first-party; the `tengu_harbor` / `allow_channels` feature gates are on; org policy allows channels (team/enterprise need `channelsEnabled: true`); the connection is not on the modern protocol era.

## Measurements

Probe server: a stdio MCP server pushing the emitter's exact message shape at fixed delays.

| Session shape | Registered? | Push to turn start | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interactive, in a PTY, `--dangerously-load-development-channels server:coordwake` | Yes, 13 ms after connect | **77 ms** (emit 19:40:13.518Z, notification receipt 19:40:13.520Z, explicit engine turn start 19:40:13.595Z) | A blocking `WARNING: Loading development channels` dialog had to be confirmed at launch. The model call then failed: the system account is at its weekly limit, so no reply was measured. |
| Headless print mode, `-p --input-format stream-json` | No | No turn for either push (1.5 s, 15 s) | The server connected, but the CLI never registered the channel. |

Current wake delivery, from `harness_shared.event_wake_deliveries` over the last 7 days:

| Channel | Delivered | delivered − created p10 / p50 / p90 | Never picked up |
|---|---|---|---|
| psu-socket-inject | 9,330 | 47 s / 59 s / 280 s | 946 (10%) |

`min_sleep_sec` averaged 60 s on those rows. The delay is the deliberate min-sleep and coalescing window plus the wait for the target session to go idle, not the transport hop, which is not recorded separately.

## Why not adopt

- **No like-for-like transport gain was measured.** The Channels emit-to-engine-turn interval is 77 ms. Current wake timings include the policy/coalescing window and waiting for an idle session; their transport hop was not separately measured. Channels also wait for the current turn to end.
- **Every launch would carry a blocking dialog**, unless our plugin is on an approved channels allowlist we do not control.
- **No headless coverage.** Headless wakes (`resume-headless`) would still need the current path.
- **The 10% never-picked-up rate is not addressed.** The CLI queue also needs an idle session.
- **It adds a second MCP server per session.**

## What would change the verdict

- The CLI accepts a local channel without the development dialog for individual accounts, or
- Channels register in headless/print mode.

## Side finding

The system OAuth account on this box (`~/.claude` credentials) reports `You've hit your weekly limit · resets Oct 25, 10pm (America/New_York)`. Sessions launched on the default system account will fail until then.
